display.purpose: The name block. Once per page, nowhere else.

headline.purpose: The section question, set as an h2. A line of dialogue, not a banner.

body.purpose: All prose, in the sans, inside a 760px measure.

label.purpose: Dates, stack lines, where-tags, hints, bar controls.

measure.purpose: Measured numbers. Always tabular so columns compare.

themes.name: dark
themes.note: Default. Warm near-black ground, cream text.

themes.name: light
themes.note: Paper ground. Accent darkened to clear 4.5:1 on paper.

themes.name: redis
themes.note: Hidden. Entered by typing a Redis command into the composer.

shadows.name: overlay-lift
shadows.purpose: The reader dialog rising from the bottom edge.

shadows.name: sheet-edge
shadows.purpose: A PDF page slot before it has rendered.

shadows.name: printed-sheet
shadows.purpose: The same slot once a page has painted, so paper reads as paper.

shadows.name: floating-control
shadows.purpose: The zoom dock hovering over the pages.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Every hover and focus transition: colour, border-color, background-color.

motion.name: turn-appear
motion.purpose: A section fading in, staggered 130ms per turn via --i. Removed entirely under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: sheet-slide
motion.purpose: The reader sheet dragging and settling.

motion.name: scene-open
motion.purpose: The view transition to the timeline, a circle opening from the click point.

motion.name: page-recede
motion.purpose: The outgoing page falling back behind that circle.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.note: Below this the hero city scene is dropped.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.note: Below this every grid collapses to one column and thumbs go full width to a 320px cap.

components.name: Bar Control
components.description: Language and theme toggles in the sticky bar. Transparent until touched.
components.css: .ds-bar-ctl { font: 400 12px/1.7 var(--font); color: var(--dim); padding: 2px 8px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 3px; background: none; cursor: pointer; transition: color 0.15s, border-color 0.15s, background-color 0.15s; } .ds-bar-ctl:hover { color: var(--fg); } .ds-bar-ctl[aria-pressed="true"] { color: var(--fg); border-color: var(--rule); background: var(--bg-2); } .ds-bar-ctl:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--claude); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 2px; }

components.name: Command Link
components.description: An inline slash command in prose. Underline goes terracotta with the text.
components.css: .ds-cmd { font: 400 13px/1.7 var(--font); color: var(--fg); background: none; border: 0; padding: 0; cursor: pointer; text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-color: var(--faint); text-underline-offset: 3px; transition: color 0.15s, text-decoration-color 0.15s; } .ds-cmd:hover { color: var(--claude); text-decoration-color: var(--claude); } .ds-cmd:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--claude); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 2px; }

components.name: Composer
components.description: The fixed command input. No box on the field itself, only a caret inside a ruled line.
components.css: .ds-composer { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 1ch; padding: 8px 12px; font: 400 14px/1.7 var(--font); background: var(--bg); border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 6px; transition: border-color 0.15s; } .ds-composer:focus-within { border-color: var(--dim); } .ds-composer__caret { color: var(--dim); } .ds-composer__input { flex: 1; min-width: 0; padding: 0; font: inherit; color: var(--fg); background: none; border: 0; outline: none; caret-color: var(--claude); } .ds-composer__input::placeholder { color: var(--faint); }

components.name: Tool Call Line
components.description: The signature line. Green names the tool, dim carries its argument; output hangs off the gutter glyph.
components.html:
Read(measurements.md)

11 lines, every one read off a test or a dashboard.
components.css: .ds-tool { margin: 0 0 0 0; padding-left: 2ch; font: 400 13px/1.7 var(--font); } .ds-tool__name { font-weight: 600; color: var(--ok); } .ds-tool__arg { color: var(--dim); } .ds-out { position: relative; margin: 6px 0 0; padding-left: 4ch; color: var(--dim); font: 400 13.5px/1.7 var(--font); } .ds-out::before { content: "\232F"; position: absolute; left: 2ch; top: 0; color: var(--faint); }

components.name: Measurement Row
components.description: A measured number and what it means. Terracotta marks the figure that matters; everything numeric is tabular.
components.html: 373→4List calls per service phase evaluation on a 20-shard serviceKubernetes operator · 2026
components.css: .ds-row { position: relative; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 140px minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 0 16px; align-items: baseline; padding-left: 4ch; font-size: 14.5px; } .ds-row::before { content: "\232F"; position: absolute; left: 2ch; top: 0; color: var(--faint); } .ds-row__num { font: 600 13.5px/1.7 var(--font); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-row__arrow { color: var(--faint); padding: 0 0.5ch; } .ds-row__n { color: var(--claude); font-weight: 600; } .ds-row__where { display: block; font: 400 12px/1.7 var(--font); color: var(--dim); }

components.name: Welcome Panel
components.description: The only container in the system, and the only place the accent draws a border. No fill.
components.html: ✻ Welcome to Seokwon Choi's portfolio.
components.css: .ds-welcome { border: 1px solid var(--claude); border-radius: 6px; padding: 14px 18px 16px; font: 400 15px/1.7 var(--font-sans); color: var(--fg); } .ds-welcome__hello { margin: 0; font-weight: 600; } .ds-spark { display: inline-block; width: 1.3em; color: var(--claude); cursor: pointer; }

components.name: Timeline Thumb
components.description: A screenshot in a timeline entry. Crops to 16/10; the border goes terracotta on hover.
components.css: .ds-thumb { width: 112px; padding: 0; border: 0; background: none; cursor: zoom-in; border-radius: 4px; } .ds-thumb__img { display: block; width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 16 / 10; object-fit: cover; border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 4px; background: var(--bg-2); transition: border-color 0.15s; } .ds-thumb:hover .ds-thumb__img { border-color: var(--claude); }

components.name: Timeline Mark
components.description: An institution's logo in a timeline entry. Never crops, never bleeds; sits on paper at 62% of its plate.
components.css: .ds-mark { display: block; width: 112px; } .ds-mark__img { display: block; width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 16 / 10; object-fit: contain; padding: 11.9% 19%; background: var(--paper); border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 4px; }

narrative.overview:
The page is one session with an agent, read top to bottom. Each section opens with the question a reader would have asked, set as a prompt line. Under it comes a tool call, and under that the output, hung off a gutter glyph. Nothing on the page pretends to be a brochure. The structure is the argument: a claim is worth what the tool call under it returned.

The temperament is quiet and precise. Monospace carries the chrome, so the page reads as instrument rather than advertisement, and the restraint is what makes the two signal colours land: a reader who has scrolled past forty lines of ink notices terracotta immediately. Density is deliberate — a 760px measure, 46px between turns, and a 1.7 line-height throughout — because the page is read once, carefully, by someone deciding whether to make a call.

Three WebGL scenes sit behind the page and never in front of it. They load only when a mount nears the viewport, hold a still frame under prefers-reduced-motion, and are aria-hidden throughout. Atmosphere is allowed; interference is not.
keyCharacteristics: Mono for chrome, sans for prose, never the reverse
Two signal colours, each with exactly one job
Flat by default; shadow means "this left the page"
Every string present in both Korean and English, one hidden by CSS
Small radii (2–6px); nothing is a pill, nothing is square by accident

rules.name: The Two-Signal Rule
rules.body: Terracotta means "a human should look here"; green means "this line is a tool call". Nothing else in the system is allowed a colour. A third accent would cost both of them their meaning.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: --faint carries real text — the cwd and loc lines, the IPA line, stack labels, the composer placeholder — so each theme's value is the minimum lift that clears 4.5:1 on that theme's own background. It was 3.12:1 on dark and 2.54:1 on light before being raised. Never darken a neutral without re-checking it.

rules.name: The Mono-First Rule
rules.body: Mono is chrome; the sans is for reading. The mono stack lists IBM Plex Sans KR before monospace on purpose: Plex Mono has no Hangul, and without that entry every Korean word in a mono run would fall to a different face mid-line.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Anything a reader might compare down a column — measurements, years, page counts, zoom percentages — carries font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.

rules.name: The Own-Column Rule
rules.body: A timeline or ledger row's text always occupies its own grid column rather than flowing around an image, so a missing picture leaves alignment untouched.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A shadow is a statement that an element is not part of the document. If it scrolls with the page, it gets a rule or a tonal step, never a shadow.

rules.name: The Clear-Space Rule
rules.body: A logo never bleeds and never crops. It sits on paper whichever theme is up, at 62% of its plate, because the air around a wordmark is part of the wordmark.

dos: Do spend terracotta on the spark, measured numbers, the caret, and interaction states — and nothing else.
Do set every numeric run in mono with tabular-nums.
Do write both the Korean and the English string into the markup and let [data-lang] hide the inactive one. Nothing re-renders on a language change.
Do keep new colours out of the token set; compose from the nine that exist.
Do check a new neutral against 4.5:1 on each theme's own background before shipping it.
Do bump the ?v=N on css/site.css in every page that links it whenever the stylesheet changes.
donts: Don't add a shadow to anything that scrolls with the document.
Don't put prose in the mono face or chrome in the sans.
Don't let a WebGL scene animate under prefers-reduced-motion, take focus, or drop its aria-hidden.
Don't crop or bleed an institution's logo; it is a mark, not a screenshot.
Don't introduce a third accent colour. Two signals is the whole system.
Don't ship a string in one language only.
